clue.text: Keep on filling 13

indicators.note: filling says the word on goes inside the other answer named by number

parts.note: the answer to 13 across, a unit of sixty minutes

explanation.surface: An instruction to keep something stuffed inside clue 13, like a crossword cross-reference command.
explanation.walkthrough: The number 13 stands for that light's answer, so 'filling' works on a word you must solve elsewhere in the grid first.
explanation.definitionFit: To keep a promise or agreement is to fulfil it faithfully, the verb sense.

clue.text: These bodies, full of revolting fat

indicators.note: revolting means turning over, so the hidden run is read backwards
full of says the letters sit inside the words These bodies

explanation.surface: A remark about bodies stuffed with disgusting fat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'full of' finds ESEBO across 'thESE BOdies'; 'revolting' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: Obesity is the state of being very overweight, so the adjective means very fat.

clue.text: Local monster of rampant shade of green

indicators.note: rampant in heraldry means rearing up, so in a down entry the pieces read from bottom to top

parts.note: a local is a nearby pub, a bar
a devil is a fiend or monster
O is a short form of of, as in o'clock

explanation.surface: A rampaging monster of a lake, perhaps, giving its name to a shade of green.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rampant' reverses BAR DEVIL O to give the answer. A 'local' is British slang for one's neighbourhood pub.
explanation.definitionFit: Olive drab is the dull brownish-green colour of military uniforms.

clue.text: Sailor called to hold this, oddly

indicators.note: to hold says the word for called contains the other letters

parts.note: rang means called on the telephone

indicators.note: oddly takes the first and third letters of the word this

explanation.surface: A seaman summoned to grasp something in an odd way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly' takes TI from 'this'; RANG holds it.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Royal Navy a rating is a non-commissioned sailor.

clue.text: Mail box shortly found in dump

indicators.note: found in says the shortened box word sits inside the word for dump

parts.note: to ditch something is to dump it

indicators.note: shortly says the box word loses its final letter

parts.note: to spar is to box in practice

explanation.surface: A mail box discovered at a rubbish dump.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mail box' reads as one postal object; split it, with 'Mail' the definition and 'box' the sparring verb that 'shortly' trims.
explanation.definitionFit: To mail a letter is to send it off, which is what dispatching does.

clue.text: In loose prose can 'e do this?

definitions.text: In loose prose can 'e do this?

indicators.note: loose says the letters of the phrase are set free and rearranged

explanation.surface: A question about whether 'e, writing in casual style, omits his aitches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loose' rearranges the fifteen letters of 'prose can 'e do this'. The clue's own 'e is written with the H dropped, illustrating the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Dropping aitches is the habit of not sounding the H at the start of words, as in 'e for he.

clue.text: Vessel extending some way down? Spooner (and farmer!) would say so

definitions.text: Vessel extending some way down? Spooner (and farmer!) would say so

indicators.note: Spooner swaps the opening sounds of two words, after the Oxford don famous for such slips

parts.note: deep means extending a long way down
a ship is a sea-going vessel

explanation.surface: A deep ship turns into a farmyard bath when Spooner, or a farmer, says it.
explanation.walkthrough: Swap the openings of DEEP SHIP. A farmer would say it too, because the result is a bath sheep are plunged into: a deep vessel of sorts.
explanation.definitionFit: A sheep dip is a deep trough of disinfectant through which farmers drive their flock.

clue.text: Some cantatas said to be very musical

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A remark that certain choral works are said to be highly musical.
explanation.definitionFit: Assai is the Italian tempo marking meaning very, as in allegro assai.

clue.text: Specially chosen guards make use of monuments

indicators.note: guards says the rearranged letters surround the word for make use of
specially suggests the letters of chosen are specially rearranged

parts.note: to tap a resource is to make use of it

explanation.surface: Hand-picked sentries exploit memorial structures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Specially' rearranges the letters of 'chosen' into CENOHS, which 'guards' wraps round the tapping word.
explanation.definitionFit: Cenotaphs are memorials to the dead buried elsewhere, a kind of war monument.

clue.text: Bluish flower that man returned to Labour guy

parts.note: he means that man

indicators.note: returned says the word for labour is read backwards

parts.note: toil is hard labour
a guy is a rope securing a tent

explanation.surface: A political tale: a man went back to the Labour party with a blue flower.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Labour' looks political but is simply hard work; 'returned' turns TOIL round.
explanation.definitionFit: Heliotrope is a plant with fragrant purple-blue blooms, also giving its name to that colour.

clue.text: Wrong hotel function

parts.note: a sin is a moral wrong
H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Something that went wrong at a hotel event.
explanation.walkthrough: 'function' suggests a party at the hotel, but it is the mathematical sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Sinh is the hyperbolic sine, a mathematical function.

clue.text: Racing driver goes around before adding nothing to this time

indicators.note: adding says the zero is attached at the end
goes around says the driver's name surrounds the word for before

parts.note: James Hunt was the 1976 Formula One world champion
ere is an old word for before
O is zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A racing driver laps the circuit before adding nothing to his time so far.
explanation.walkthrough: 'before' looks like a link of order, but it supplies the archaic word ERE; 'goes around' and 'adding' do the assembling.
explanation.definitionFit: Hereunto is a formal word meaning up to this point or until now.

clue.text: Stand to get dressing in pub

indicators.note: in says the dressing word sits inside the pub abbreviation

parts.note: PH is the map abbreviation for public house
lint is a soft fabric used for dressing wounds

explanation.surface: Standing at the bar to have a wound bandaged in the pub.
explanation.definitionFit: A plinth is the base or pedestal on which a statue stands.

clue.text: Endless suffering will stop over time

indicators.note: will stop says the over abbreviation plugs a gap in the shortened word
endless says the word for suffering loses its last letter

parts.note: hurt is pain or suffering
O is the cricket abbreviation for over

explanation.surface: A hopeful promise that pain will cease in due course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Endless' cuts HURT to HUR; 'will stop' puts O into it.
explanation.definitionFit: An hour is a unit of time of sixty minutes.

clue.text: Spy runs through videotape, cutting date out

indicators.note: out says the letters are knocked out of order and rearranged

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: An agent fast-forwards a recording, editing out the date stamp.
explanation.walkthrough: R plus VIDEOTAPE, less D ('cutting date'), rearranged by 'out' gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An operative is a secret agent working in the field.

clue.text: Engineer happier about good inscription

indicators.note: about says the rearranged letters surround the good abbreviation
to engineer is to contrive, so the letters of happier are reworked

explanation.surface: An engineer, cheerier now, thinks about good things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Engineer' rearranges HAPPIER into EPIRAPH; 'about' puts G inside.
explanation.definitionFit: An epigraph is an inscription on a building or statue, or a quotation heading a book.

clue.text: Author and press may be heard now

indicators.note: may be heard says the words are spoken rather than spelt

parts.note: an author is a writer, and to press down is to weigh

explanation.surface: A writer and the newspapers may be listened to now.
explanation.walkthrough: WRITER plus WEIGH said quickly sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Right away means immediately, at once, without delay.

clue.text: To catch wearing stupid hair colour

indicators.note: wearing says the brutish word has the catching word on the inside of it

parts.note: a brute is an unthinking, stupid creature
to net a fish is to catch it

explanation.surface: Getting caught out wearing a silly hair dye.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wearing' reads as dressed in, but here the outer word wears the inner one like a garment.
explanation.definitionFit: Brunette describes dark brown hair, a hair shade, or a woman who has it.

clue.text: Save one acre east of woman's dried plant collections

indicators.note: east of in an across answer means placed to the right, after the woman's word

parts.note: her means belonging to a woman
bar and save both mean except
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A woman's land, except one acre, used for drying plants.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Save' is not rescue but the preposition meaning except, hence BAR.
explanation.definitionFit: A herbarium is a systematically arranged collection of dried, pressed botanical specimens.

clue.text: Square blocks hold back torrent

indicators.note: blocks says the square abbreviation sits in the reversed word like a barrier
back says the word for hold is turned round

parts.note: to hug someone is to hold them
S stands for square, as in the abbreviation for square measures

explanation.surface: Square concrete blocks stem a rushing flood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns HUG to GUH and 'blocks' sets S inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A gush is a sudden rushing outpouring of liquid, like a torrent.

clue.text: Level crossing not good, but perhaps standard?

indicators.note: crossing says the level word straddles the word for not good

parts.note: par means equal or level
ill means bad, not good

explanation.surface: A railway level crossing that is unsafe but perhaps typical.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Level crossing' reads as railway infrastructure; it is PAR going across ILL.
explanation.definitionFit: A standard can be an upright pole or post, of which a column is one example.

clue.text: Sprint is complete with X

parts.note: something complete with an item has it
X is the Roman numeral ten

explanation.surface: A race that comes with a marked cross, like a sprint track with an X.
explanation.walkthrough: X is not a cross or a kiss but the Roman ten.
explanation.definitionFit: To sprint is to move very fast, to hurry or rush.

clue.text: Ultimately, what takes little time to post?

definitions.text: Ultimately, what takes little time to post?

indicators.note: ultimately points to the last letter of the word what

parts.note: wee is Scottish for little

explanation.surface: A question about what is quick to put online.
explanation.walkthrough: 'takes' links the end of 'what' to WEE and T. The whole clue also describes the answer: a short message posted online in moments.
explanation.definitionFit: A tweet is a brief message posted on the social platform X, formerly Twitter.

clue.text: After outing they emptied church altarpiece

parts.note: a trip is an outing

indicators.note: emptied means the middle letters of they are removed, leaving the outer pair

explanation.surface: After a day trip, visitors cleared out of the church to see the altarpiece.
explanation.definitionFit: A triptych is a three-panelled painting, typically hung behind an altar.

clue.text: The evidence initially hidden by detectives is mentioned

indicators.note: hidden by says those letters are concealed inside the detectives abbreviation

parts.note: CID is the Criminal Investigation Department, British plain-clothes detectives

indicators.note: initially takes the opening letters of The and evidence

explanation.surface: Evidence concealed by police detectives gets referred to.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hidden by' is a container signal here, not a hidden-word one: the opening letters picked by 'initially' sit inside the detectives.
explanation.definitionFit: Something cited is quoted or referred to, which is to say mentioned.

clue.text: Every second of this will skip gentle increase

indicators.note: every second of says take the second letter of each of the next four words

explanation.surface: Skipping every other moment makes for a gentle rise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gentle increase' reads as the definition, but 'gentle' supplies a letter; the definition is just 'increase'.
explanation.definitionFit: A hike is a sharp rise, as in a price or wage increase.

clue.text: Forget what 'sexy' is about? The will to get excited

indicators.note: about says the word for sexy is turned round

parts.note: sexy means hot

indicators.note: to get excited says the letters of The will are stirred up

explanation.surface: A dismissive shrug about sexiness, and an excitable will.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' reverses HOT to TOH; 'to get excited' rearranges THE WILL.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying to hell with something is dismissing it, telling yourself to forget it.

clue.text: They don't believe you have to cook chickens

parts.note: to heat food is to cook it
hens are female chickens

explanation.surface: Unbelievers are told they must cook the poultry.
explanation.definitionFit: Heathens are people without religious faith, non-believers.

clue.text: Capital city regularly crossed by hard ground

indicators.note: crossed by says those letters lie across the inside of the shuffled hard
ground means crushed, so the letters of hard are broken up and rearranged
regularly takes alternate letters of city, the second and fourth

explanation.surface: A capital city with hard ground running through it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ground' rearranges the letters of 'hard' as RADH. 'Capital city' wants to be the whole definition, but 'city' is the word 'regularly' picks from.
explanation.definitionFit: Riyadh is the capital of Saudi Arabia.
